**F22-D146 is answered for the tested D-162 cadence:** dual/IPv4 1280 indexes **44 and 46 both PASS**. All three unchanged serving predicates pass: dual age **0.739651 s**, IPv6 **6.849400 s**, IPv4 **1.441758 s**, each below 15 s with generation 74, current incarnation, forwarding enabled and no reasons. No serving read fails on age, so there is no late enqueue/attempt/acceptance stage to attribute in this run. [Serving reports and their exact enqueue/attempt joins](F24-serving-read-records.json) retain `interval_elapsed` for all three. All nine native windows retain 18 stored observations, 18 enqueues and 18 submission attempts; every stored report has its enqueue and accepted attempt, and no in-window enqueue is absent from storage. There are no malformed receipts or overwritten native-row exports. This closes the cadence finding for this measurement; it does not alter the strict bound, prove an unconditional scheduling SLA, or change the 30 s product default.

Every row retains the agent-facing control route and TCP boundary views. This does not measure the proxy’s upstream connection or prove the absence of every transport event between samples. Overwrite detection and surviving suffix duration are in each row’s log evidence.

## AT02 closed recovery

[Original closed Apply, renewal, populated lease and serving Apply](F24-AT02-closed-recovery-trace.json); [deny-all/loss accounting](F24-AT02-recovery.json). Every report candidate retains its documented enqueue reason and all observed attempt receipts; this recovery needed one accepted attempt.

| Producer / closed Apply | Renewal / serving Apply | Populated lease | Deny-all after closed Apply (ms) / losses | Apply plus wait (ms) / losses | Report candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9879ce69-34b6-4fa6-9165-cb4619bc9fde / 540 | 545 / 546 | 4b88acc1-5ff1-4618-9f40-6f1a4f06064c (generation 14, members 1) | 187.30883 / 7 | 304.961112 / 13 | 1 |

The one closed recovery is producer `9879ce69-34b6-4fa6-9165-cb4619bc9fde`: closed Apply **540**, renewal request **545**, populated generation-14 lease `4b88acc1-5ff1-4618-9f40-6f1a4f06064c`, serving Apply **546**. The renewal starts **66.406460 ms** after closed Apply ends; exactly one request and zero baseline writes lie before serving. Closed report `01a1a782-6b90-74a8-bcd6-c9a06650a2ec` is enqueued at **17:01:44.722Z**, observed at **17:01:44.720284884Z**, with **`closed_recovery_binding`**. Its attempt 1 finishes accepted at **17:01:44.730Z** (duration 6 ms; enqueue to completion **8 ms**). The enqueue and submission are lines **207 and 208** of `AT02-interim-170257/node-agent.log`; the exact documented fields and byte pins are retained in the trace. The deny-all interval after closed Apply is **187.308830 ms / seven losses**; Apply plus wait is **304.961112 ms / 13 losses**. These are measured intervals, not an outage ceiling. A later usage restart overwrites the agent log; `AT02-interim-170257/node-agent.log` preserves this enqueue and attempt. The final AT02 node export retains a **423.919857555 s** suffix of the **915.480883769 s** case envelope; the prefix without lines in that final export is **491.561026214 s**, with earlier segments preserved by interim exports. [All snapshot coverage and pins](F24-log-coverage.json). The prior run also had seven deny-all losses and 13 Apply-plus-wait losses; this combined measurement cannot assign the timing/generation differences to one of the merged changes. Report correlation uses the unique `closed_recovery_binding` observation between the producer-anchored closed-Apply end and serving-Apply end, then joins the accepted attempt by report ID. It does not assume an undocumented internal recovery identifier.

The current run had zero suite/case admission sleeps.
